title: Decision Lattice — sketch for multi-model/tool coordinator
content:
Topline
- Quick sketch: "Decision Lattice" is a runtime decision layer that composes model variants and external tools (retrievers, calculators, web-search, private knowledge agents) per-request using a compact scoring lattice. Goal: robust, cost-aware, latency-conscious selection that degrades gracefully and is explainable to product owners.

Motivation / problem statements (raw)
- Customers ask for predictable behavior when a heavy model or a tool is unavailable—current fallbacks are ad-hoc.
- We want consistent SLAs for apps that mix generation + tool calls (e.g., summary + DB lookup).
- Platform should be able to trade off cost vs. accuracy at route-level and per-session with simple knobs.

Design constraints / desiderata
- Pluggable: decision lattice should accept new model variants and new tools without changing core logic.
- Fast scoring: decision must add negligible latency (p99 budget << 5ms ideally).
- Explainability: return a short rationale tag in response metadata (why chosen, which fallback used).
- Policy-driven: route owners can provide policies (e.g., prefer private models for PII, avoid heavy models for high-QPS).
- Observability: per-decision metrics (score breakdown, simulated regret vs. gold model).

Core idea (very rough)
- Inputs: request features (route, user tier, input token length, latency-SLO, privacy flags, hint tokens from prompt), runtime signals (current capacity, queueing delay), model/tool catalog (capabilities, cost, avg-latency, privacy level).
- Scoring: each candidate (model-only, model+tool, tool-only pipeline) gets multi-axis score vector: {expected-latency, expected-cost, capability-match, privacy-ok, historical-quality}.
- Lattice: discretize axes into tiers and apply policy functions that map to allowed candidates. If multiple candidates pass, pick minimum expected-cost subject to latency SLO and capability threshold.
- Fallback chaining: if candidate fails at runtime (timeout/error), walk predetermined fallback chain; record event and try next best candidate.

Example user stories
1) As a product owner for SummarizeRoute, I want the runtime to prefer the private 7B quantized model for documents flagged private, falling back to hosted 13B if private pool is saturated, so my app never leaks customer text.
  - Acceptance: request metadata includes selected_candidate: "private-7b:v2" and fallback_used flag when applicable; routing respects private flag 100% of the time when capacity available.
2) As an ML engineer, I want to run an A/B where 10% of traffic uses a reranker step (retriever->reranker->gen) while 90% uses a single-model pipeline, so we can measure value-of-reranker.
  - Acceptance: lattice can be configured with sampling policy per route, and metrics show cost/quality delta.
3) As an infra engineer, I want a graceful, observable degradation path when GPU pool latency > threshold to automatically move requests to cheaper CPU models with a notice to the app, so SLAs are preserved.
  - Acceptance: automated policy detects latency spike and flips preferred candidates; events emitted to console and logs.

Configuration surface (initial minimal API sketch)
- RoutePolicy: {
    "priority_axes": ["latency","cost","privacy","quality"],
    "thresholds": {"latency_ms": 300, "privacy": "strict"},
    "sampling": {"candidate_a": 0.1},
    "fallback_order": ["private-7b","hosted-13b","synth-llm-lite"]
  }
Notes: store as YAML/JSON in Console; Console UI can present easy toggles (aggressive-cost-saving slider).

Observability / metrics
- Per-decision: chosen_candidate, reason_code (policy_match / fallback / sampling), score_vector, simulated_regret (compare to baseline gold if available).
- Aggregates: cost per 1k requests, latency p50/p95/p99 per candidate, fallback-rate.
- Alerts: fallback-rate > X% for route triggers investigation.

Experiment ideas / evals
- Offline replay: given historical requests, simulate lattice choices and compute average cost and quality vs. current policy.
- Small live canary: 1% traffic with lattice -> compare user-visible regressions.
- Bandit-lite: allow lattice to explore lower-cost candidates slowly and compute uplift/regret.

Data needs
- Per-candidate historical quality: need label sets or heuristics (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-sim). Start with sampled human evals for critical routes.
- Latency and cost models per candidate: runtime histograms, and simple cost model per token + fixed tool cost.

Open questions / risks
- How to calibrate "capability-match" across different model architectures? Need a small eval matrix per route.
- Cold-start: new model variants have no history and may be chosen incorrectly; need safe default (conservative prior).
- Complexity for product teams: too many knobs -> confusion. UI must present simple presets (conservative, balanced, frugal).
- Security and privacy: ensure that route-level policies override any sampling that could route PII through non-private models.

Next steps (concrete short-term)
- Spike: implement a prototype scoring lambda that runs in front of existing router. Feed it a fake catalog of 4 candidates and 5k historical requests (local sim). Owner: Talia (dev), pair: Ravi. ETA: 2 weeks.
- Instrument: decide minimal telemetry fields to emit; add tags to existing router logs. Owner: Mika. ETA: 1 week.
- UX: sketch Console toggles and policy presets. Owner: Evelyn. ETA: 1 sprint.

Parking-lot ideas (quick jots)
- Expose per-session affinity to bias candidate selection (user prefers terse replies -> lower-cost models).
- Weighting as a small neural net that learns to predict cost+quality tradeoff per route (longer-term).
- "Simulated regret" dashboard that lets PMs see how much cheaper they'd be at X% quality loss.

Notes to self (loose)
- Keep decision-core tiny; heavy lifting in catalog service and offline sims.
- Propose a simple reason_code taxonomy for downstream billing/alerts.
- Try implementing fallback chain as immutable vector in RoutePolicy so rollout is safe.

References / links to check later
- INF-4823 (existing router refactor ticket)
- Decision-tree literature (bandit/graph search flavors)
- Prior notes: Ravi's "turn-economy" doc (might have overlap)

End of sketch — rough but actionable. Will flesh into PRD if spike shows promise.
